history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - this is a Roman Catholic church. IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV name 'Roman Catholic Church' is generic; no official parish list could be consulted to pin a specific parish in Lunglei. This record is provisionally mapped to Sacred Heart Church at Venglai, Lunglei, the only named Catholic parish church in Lunglei town found in place listings (verify - confirm this is the intended parish). The Catholic Church in Mizoram belongs to the Diocese of Aizawl (Latin Rite, ecclesiastical province of Shillong): established as the Apostolic Prefecture of Haflong in 1952, raised as the Diocese of Silchar in 1969 and renamed Aizawl in 1996, with Christ the King Cathedral in Aizawl and St. Joseph as patron; the current bishop is Stephen Rotluanga, C.S.C., the first Mizo bishop (from 2001). The diocese reported 32 parishes and about 41,067 Catholics in 2020 (verify) - a small minority in a state over 85% Christian, mostly Presbyterian and Baptist. Catholicism in Mizoram grew out of the 1919 Mizo revival and is strongest in education and healthcare: by 2020 the Church ran 53 educational institutions in the state (verify), including schools at Kolasib, Lunglei and Mamit. The Catholic community in Lunglei is served around parish churches and institutions such as Sacred Heart School at Venglai (verify affiliation and parish boundary). If the dataset owner has a different Lunglei parish in mind, the parish name should be corrected.

name: Roman Catholic Church
town_description: Lunglei is the second-largest town of Mizoram and the headquarters of Lunglei district, about 165-200 km south of Aizawl. 'Lunglei' means 'bridge of rock', from a rock formation near Nghasih, a tributary of the Tlawng river. The town's religious life is overwhelmingly Protestant (Presbyterian and Baptist); the Catholic community is small but runs institutions including Sacred Heart School at Venglai locality. Other landmarks include Saikuti Hall, Thuamluaia Mual football stadium and the nearby Khawnglung Wildlife Sanctuary.
